strings.ui.here_you_can_tell_yt_dlp_to_download_:
Here you can tell yt-dlp to download only a section (or multiple sections) of the media. Define a section by specifying a start point and an end point, then add it to the list. The time points are in the format <bold color=0x>[hour:][minute:]second</>.

For example, <bold color=0x>54</> means second 54, <bold color=0x>9:54</> means minute 9 second 54, and <bold color=0x>1:9:54</> means hour 1 minute 9 second 54.
To indicate the end of the media, put <bold color=0x>0</> in the "to" field or leave it blank. 

The downloading of sections is done through FFmpeg (which is much slower), and each section is downloaded to its own file.

When the settings are saved, any incomplete queue items are also saved,
except for those with the "error" status. This option lets you also save the
items with the "error" status, which can be useful when a download fails
due to connection issues, but can be resumed later.
strings.ui.this_option_lets_you_override_your_vi:
This option lets you override your video codec preference, in the case when a video
has format 616 available (which has the "premium" bitrate). For example, if you're
downloading a 1080p video and you prefer the H264 codec, this option will override
that codec preference by requesting format 616 from yt-dlp (with the argument
"-f 616+ba").
strings.ui.forces_yt_dlp_to_use_the_android_clie:
Forces yt-dlp to use the Android client for extracting the video by passing
"<bold>--extractor-args youtube:player_client=android</>". This can be useful
because some formats are only available to the Android client.

However, be aware of the warning from yt-dlp:
"<bold>Android client formats are broken and may yield HTTP Error 403</>"
strings.ui.if_several_different_formats_have_the:
If several different formats have the same resolution,
download the one with the highest framerate.
strings.ui.when_yt_dlp_finishes_downloading_all_:
When yt-dlp finishes downloading all the files associated with a queue item,
it performs actions on the files referred to as "post-processing". These actions
can be a number of things, depending on the context, and on the options used.

Sometimes this post-processing phase can take a long time, so this setting
makes the program automatically start the next queue item when processing
takes longer that 3 seconds.
strings.ui.this_option_pads_the_index_numbers_in:
This option pads the index numbers in the filenames of playlist videos
with zeroes, when the playlist contains more than 9 videos. This allows
the filenames to be sorted properly when viewed in a file manager (for
example, <bold>"2 - name"</> comes after <bold>"14 - name"</> in the sort order, but
<bold>"02 - name"</> comes before <bold>"14 - name"</>).

This feature works by automatically editing the "Playlist indexing" string
defined above, as long as it contains <bold>"%(playlist_index)d"</>.

An appropriate amount of zeroes is added, according to the size of the
playlist (if it has tens of videos, up to one zero; if it has hundreds of
videos, up to two zeroes; etc).
strings.ui.put_playlist_videos_in_a_subfolder_of:
Put playlist videos in a subfolder of the output folder, using the
playlist title as the name of the subfolder.

This works by automatically prepending <bold>"%(playlist_title)s\"</> to the
output template defined above, whenever a playlist is downloaded

Since v1.9, this setting also applies to channels and channel tabs.

Since v2.1, this setting also applies to Bandcamp albums (prepends
<bold>"%(artist)s\%(album)s\"</> to the output template).
strings.ui.if_this_option_is_checked_whenever_th:
If this option is checked, whenever the main window receives the input focus,
any URL in the clipboard will be automatically added to the queue (if it's not
already there). This only works for a single URL (if you have a multi-line list of
URLs, you'll have to add it manually).
strings.ui.you_can_provide_a_custom_file_name_fo:
You can provide a custom file name for a queue item by selecting
<bold>Set file name for item #</> from the queue menu, or by pressing <bold>F2</>.
This name is "custom" because it overrides the output template
defined in the settings.

If you check this option, then if a queue item has a custom file name,
it will be shown in the "Media title" column instead of the media title.
strings.ui.download_the_best_video_with_the_larg:
Download the best video with the largest resolution available that is
not higher than the selected value. Resolution is determined using the
smallest dimension, so this works correctly for vertical videos as well.
strings.ui.when_a_queue_item_finishes_the_progra:
When a queue item finishes, the program automatically starts the next one.
This setting lets you make it start the next two or more items (up to 10).

Does not limit the number of manually started queue items (you can have
more than 10 concurrent downloads if you want, but you have to start
the ones after the 10th manually).
strings.ui.the_output_template_tells_yt_dlp_how_:
The output template tells yt-dlp how to name the downloaded files.
It's a powerful way to compose the output file name, allowing many 
characteristics of the downloaded media to be incorporated 
into the name. To learn how to use it, see the documentation at 
<bold>https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#output-template</>
strings.ui.this_is_a_string_that_the_program_opt:
This is a string that the program optionally incorporates into the 
output template defined above, only when downloading 
YouTube playlists. It is prepended to the output template string, 
so with default values, the result would look like this:

<bold>"%(playlist_index)d - %(title)s.%(ext)s"</>

This output template produces filenames that look like this:

<bold>1 - title.ext
2 - title.ext
3 - title.ext</>

Leave blank if you don't want playlist videos to be numbered.
strings.ui.a_container_format_allows_multiple_da:
A container format allows multiple data streams to be embedded
into a single file. A media container is a file that can contain multiple 
video and/or audio streams. The codec with which the video and 
audio streams are encoded affects which container they can fit in.

For example, the MPEG-4 video container format (<bold>.mp4</> file) can 
contain audio streams encoded with the <bold>mp4a</> codec, but doesn't
support audio encoded with the <bold>opus</> codec (which yt-dlp considers
to be the better of the two).

For that reason, if you select <bold>mp4</> as the preferred video container,
you must select <bold>m4a</> as the preferred audio container. Otherwise,
yt-dlp will be forced to merge the streams into an <bold>.mkv</> file instead
of an <bold>.mp4</> file (when combining an <bold>.mp4</> video-only format with
an incompatible audio-only format).
strings.ui.tell_yt_dlp_to_use_a_proxy_server_thi:
Tell yt-dlp to use a proxy server (this passes <bold>--proxy</> to yt-dlp)

	HTTP proxy:  <bold>IP_ADDRESS:PORT</>

	SOCKS proxy:  <bold>socks5://IP_ADDRESS:PORT</>

	SOCKS proxy with authentication:  <bold>socks5://USER:PASS@IP_ADDRESS:PORT</>
strings.ui.in_the_context_of_digital_video_and_a:
In the context of digital video and audio, a codec is a processing algorithm
used to compress data, and the process of compressing data with a codec
is called "encoding".

A website like YouTube may offer multiple formats that use the same
container, but different codecs, so specifying a preferred codec can prevent
unwanted formats from being downloaded.
strings.ui.here_you_can_tell_the_program_where_t:
Here you can tell the program where to put the FFmpeg files when
it updates FFmpeg (via Settings->Updater). If the folder you choose
is not the yt-dlp folder, the program will offer to set up yt-dlp
(via config file) to look for the FFmpeg files in that folder.
<bold>.\ </>means the program folder (where ytdlp-interface.exe is located).
strings.ui.bold_means_the_program_folder_where_y: <bold>.\ </>means the program folder (where ytdlp-interface.exe is located).
strings.ui.when_a_url_is_added_to_the_queue_the_:
When a URL is added to the queue, the program uses yt-dlp to get info about it,
and about the media that can be downloaded from it. When adding multiple
URLs to the queue (either by pasting a list of URLs or by splitting a playlist), the
program uses multiple concurrent yt-dlp instances, up to a maximum of 4 by
default. You can increase this number up to the number of logical processors on
your system, but you should be aware of a few considerations before you do.

First, if you're downloading a lot from YouTube, you should consider the
possibility that you might get banned for making too many requests too quickly.
I don't know how likely that is to happen, but I know it's possible.

Second, yt-dlp eats a lot of CPU resources for what it does, because Python is an
interpreted language (yt-dlp.exe contains the Python interpreter, which runs the
yt-dlp program). It's possible to max out your CPU utilization by increasing this
number, and the responsiveness of the interface may be lowered.
strings.ui.additional_options_for_the_bold_cooki:
Additional options for the <bold>--cookies-from-browser</> argument,
in the format <bold>[:PROFILE][::CONTAINER]</>.

The text you type is passed to yt-dlp as is, without any validation.
strings.ui.the_program_will_use_bold_cookies_fro:
The program will use <bold>--cookies-from-browser</> when downloading
and when getting data for a URL.

This will cause yt-dlp to automatically authenticate with the website
you're downloading from, if you're logged into it in your browser.

Use the drop-down list to select which browser to get cookies from,
and type any additional options in the textbox.

WARNING: Due to recent changes to how Chrome handles cookies,
this will probably not work with Chrome.

strings.ui.when_updating_ffmpeg_the_program_will:
When updating FFmpeg, the program will put the FFmpeg files in the folder you selected. There's just one problem though, the folder you selected is not the same as the folder that contains yt-dlp.exe, so yt-dlp will not know how to find the FFmpeg files.

[ Yes ] To fix that, a configuration file (yt-dlp.conf) containing the argument "--ffmpeg-location" can be created in the yt-dlp folder.

[ No ] Or, the program can pass "--ffmpeg-location" to yt-dlp through the command line.

strings.web.context.source_note: Only available items can be selected. Full information shows selected titles and unavailable reasons.
strings.web.context.empty_naming: Choose naming fields or enter a template.
strings.web.context.naming_note: The example uses preview data. Downloads use the media metadata. Save output settings after applying naming.
strings.web.context.settings_appearance: Language applies after restart. Other saved appearance settings apply immediately.
strings.web.context.settings_queue: Scheduler settings apply immediately. Recovery policies apply on next launch. Output defaults apply to future tasks.
strings.web.context.settings_network: Saved network and authentication settings apply to the next parse or download. Active operations retain their settings.
strings.web.context.settings_sponsor: Marking retains segments; removal changes the content. Saved choices apply to the next download.
strings.web.context.settings_presets: Application presets save download defaults and the existing seven settings groups, excluding appearance, queue and runtime logs.
strings.web.context.draft_note: Preview does not save. Apply or save to submit changes.
strings.web.context.detail_note: View full content in the central workspace. Back and Cancel keep their existing behavior.
strings.web.context.queue_note: Select a task to view status, output and recent logs.
strings.web.single_url: Paste or drop one media URL
strings.web.polish.start_hint: Start waiting, stopped and retryable failed tasks in this scope using the existing scheduler.
strings.web.polish.stop_group_hint: Stop active group tasks and mark waiting group tasks as stopped.
strings.web.polish.copy_all: Copy current processing options to entire queue…
strings.web.polish.selection_blocked: {count} selected tasks cannot be removed now. Wait for active processing or refresh, or stop the tasks first.
strings.web.polish.edit_unavailable: Some selected tasks cannot be edited. Stop active tasks or wait for refresh to finish.
strings.web.polish.group_parent_only: Collection children cannot move to a group independently. Select their collection instead.
strings.web.polish.preview_blocked: This scope contains unavailable tasks. The operation cannot proceed.
strings.web.polish.preview_core: Actual state is checked again on execution. The result reports affected and ignored counts. Removal deletes queue records; downloaded files are retained.
strings.web.polish.reason_collection: The collection is not fully complete; this child is retained
strings.web.polish.delete_group:
Delete group “{name}”?
Its {count} objects will return to Ungrouped. Tasks and downloaded files are retained.
strings.web.polish.format_help: Choose the output container or audio format.
strings.web.polish.video_quality_help: The resolution limit uses the existing stream selection rules.
strings.web.polish.audio_quality_help: High quality is the default. Retained original parameters show their actual source.
strings.web.polish.processing_m4a_native: Prefer native M4A audio, with other available audio as fallback. Conversion to M4A is not forced.
strings.web.polish.processing_m4a_convert: Output audio as M4A; the backend converts when needed.
strings.web.polish.processing_mp4: Select video and audio and merge using the existing MP4 rules.
strings.web.polish.processing_video_container: Use the existing {format} merging and remuxing rules.
strings.web.polish.processing_original: Use existing stream selection without specifying container conversion.
strings.web.polish.processing_audio: Extract audio and process output using the existing {format} rules.
strings.web.polish.processing_raw: The format currently follows custom arguments. Editing the format or strategy applies the choices here.
strings.web.polish.format_fallback: {before} is unavailable for this content type. The existing default {after} is now selected.
strings.web.polish.manual_quality_help: Manual stream choices take precedence. Quality preferences apply to automatic selection.
strings.web.polish.processing_manual: Output the chosen formats and tracks using the existing multi-audio container rules.
strings.web.polish.advanced_inherited: Custom arguments are enabled. Unedited fields retain original parameters; editing a field applies its setting here. Check the preview for the combined arguments.
strings.web.polish.retries_help: Control retries after a failed download. Default and retained original arguments keep the existing rules.
strings.web.polish.fragments_help: Control fragment concurrency within one task. This does not change how many queue tasks run at once.
strings.web.polish.rate_help: Zero or empty means unlimited. Unedited fields retain existing custom rate arguments.
strings.web.polish.chapters_help: Ignore, embed, or split chapters. Results depend on chapters provided by the source.
strings.web.polish.keyframes_help: Force keyframes at cuts. This requires re-encoding and takes longer.
strings.web.polish.keyframes_without_sections: No separate time ranges are set. This option applies at cuts and requires re-encoding.
strings.web.polish.write_time_help: Use file write time when enabled, or media server time when disabled.
strings.web.polish.live_start_help: Applies to live sources. Downloading from the start depends on yt-dlp and the site.
strings.web.polish.keep_files_help: Keep existing files with the same name using the downloader's current overwrite rules.
strings.web.polish.single_video_help: When parsing a collection link, download only the current video. Existing selected collection children are unchanged.
